hints.title: Cumulative Shift Reduction
hints.text: Left shifts decrease the starting index while right shifts increase it.

hints.title: Modulo Normalization
hints.text: Compute the net right shift modulo the string length to handle circular wrapping in constant time.

hints.title: Single Slice Extraction
hints.text: Slice string s using the normalized shift offset instead of performing repeated character movements.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def stringShift(self, s: str, shift: list[list[int]]) -> str:
        n = len(s)
        net = sum(amt if d == 1 else -amt for d, amt in shift) % n
        return s[-net:] + s[:-net]
```

variables: S: number of operations in shift
complexity.notes: Summing shift offsets takes O(S) time and constructing the final rotated string takes O(N) time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Executing physical shifts one-by-one leads to redundant string allocations and O(S * N) execution.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Consolidating net shift algebraically minimizes buffer copies to a single pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Modular arithmetic reduction aggregating transformations before string manipulation.
